title: US Q2 prelim unit labor costs +1.3% vs +2.1% expected
description: Prior was 2.3% Productivity +1.4% vs +0.6% expected Prior productivity was +0.8% This isn't really a useful report because productivity is so hard to measure and it's often revised many times. In theory, unit labor costs are a critical inflation number but it's rarely a market mover because measuring it is so variable quarter-to-quarter. The dollar has much bigger questions to answer at the moment with all the intervention in the yen. The Treasury market also doesn't like what it's been hearing
claude_impact_reason: Softer unit labor costs with stronger productivity is a mildly disinflationary combination, marginally supportive of cut pricing and gold; more notable is the embedded flag of heavy yen intervention and an unsettled Treasury market, which is a dollar-confidence/liquidity channel worth monitoring.
historical_impact_basis: Productivity/ULC is rarely a standalone gold mover due to revision noise, but FX-intervention and Treasury-stress backdrops have historically transmitted to gold via dollar and term-premium channels.
